title: Petra and the Letters
premise: Dominic Zhou, a wedding planner whose own engagement ended in silence, has spent ten years anonymously answering letters left in a lighthouse mailbox on the island of Merrow's Reach—letters written by a stranger signing as 'P.' When Petra Lindqvist, the letter writer herself, inherits her grandmother's cottage next door and arrives to restore it, Dominic must hide both his identity and his growing feelings. As the last ferry of the season approaches, Petra discovers his secret through a misdelivered reply, and Dominic must choose between the safety of invisibility and a love that demands he be seen. He lets her stay past the last train, they catch the final ferry together, and he answers one last letter signed with his real name.
about_author: Juniper Nakamura is a former stationery shop owner who wrote letters to strangers for years before turning to fiction. She lives on a small coastal island where the ferries stop running every November, and she swears this is unrelated.

chapters.title: The Mailbox at the End of the Pier
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. He plans a flawless wedding for clients who remind him painfully of his own broken engagement, then retreats to the lighthouse mailbox where, as an anonymous volunteer, he has answered strangers' letters for a decade. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as routine.

chapters.title: Letter, Unsigned
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. She inherits her grandmother's crumbling cottage and finds a shoebox of ten years of replies from someone called only 'the Keeper.' She decides to move to the island permanently. Emotional beat: grief becoming curiosity.

chapters.title: Next Door
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A moving truck arrives beside his workshop; the new neighbor is sharp-tongued, paint-stained, and asks too many questions about the lighthouse. He lies smoothly and hates himself for it. Emotional beat: first spark of unease and attraction.

chapters.title: Ten Years of 'Yours, P.'
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Reading the letters chronologically, she realizes the Keeper knew her grandmother, and that the correspondence carried her family through bankruptcy and bereavement. She writes a new letter asking who he really was. Emotional beat: hunger for connection.

chapters.title: The Wedding That Isn't
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A client cancels mid-ceremony rehearsal; Dominic talks the couple into honesty instead of spectacle, surprising himself. Petra witnesses it and sees something kind beneath his armor. Emotional beat: a crack in the wall.

chapters.title: Storm Damage
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. A storm floods the cottage; Dominic shows up unasked with tarps and soup. Working side by side, they trade half-truths about why people leave islands and why people stay. Emotional beat: reluctant intimacy.

chapters.title: The Reply He Shouldn't Write
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The new letter from 'P' sits unanswered for weeks because he recognizes her handwriting from a work order she left. Writing back would mean lying to her face by mail. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into fear of discovery.

chapters.title: Island Politics
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The town council, led by the wealthy Harrow family, moves to demolish the lighthouse and its mailbox for a resort development. Petra organizes opposition; Dominic stays conspicuously neutral. Emotional beat: her idealism against his caution.

chapters.title: What the Ferry Schedule Knows
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. He checks the autumn ferry timetable—an old habit marking when the island empties—and realizes Petra intends to winter over. Everything he's hidden has a deadline now. Emotional beat: dread with a countdown.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Ledger
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. In the cottage attic she finds her grandmother's ledger showing monthly payments to 'D.Z., keeper's fund'—the anonymous replies were paid for, sustained, personal. She confronts Dominic; he denies everything too quickly. Emotional beat: betrayal's first cold draft.

chapters.title: The Harrow Offer
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Edmund Harrow offers Dominic a lucrative contract planning the resort's opening gala if he'll quietly withdraw support from the lighthouse campaign. Money plus anonymity versus everything Petra stands for. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a tailored suit.

chapters.title: Midnight at the Lighthouse
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Unable to sleep, she catches Dominic leaving a letter in the mailbox at midnight. He doesn't see her. She reads the return address label before he seals it: his own name. Emotional beat: revelation, quiet and devastating.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Workshop
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Petra lays the ledger and the letters on his worktable. Dominic confesses: the decade of letters began as his penance after his fiancée left, funded by Petra's grandmother, whom he'd once failed. Emotional beat: truth as both wound and relief.

chapters.title: The Gala
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. He plans Harrow's gala flawlessly while the demolition vote looms, telling himself neutrality is integrity. Petra attends, distant and polite, and he understands what he's chosen. Emotional beat: success tasting like ash.

chapters.title: Vote of the Assembly
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The council votes; the lighthouse survives by two votes because Dominic, at the last moment, publicly testifies about what the mailbox meant to grieving islanders—exposing his secret role entirely. Emotional beat: redemption bought with exposure.

chapters.title: After the Vote
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Publicly known now, he expects gratitude or anger; instead Petra says the worst part wasn't the lie but that he let her grieve alone believing no one answered. She asks for space. Emotional beat: the cost of honesty arriving late.

chapters.title: Empty Mailbox
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. She restores the cottage, declines Harrow's buyout of her land, and writes one final letter she doesn't send: not forgiveness, not goodbye, just the question of whether he ever believed anything he wrote. Emotional beat: love refusing to be simple.

chapters.title: The Last Train
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. His mainland client—the gala couple—summons him off-island; the last train connection leaves the morning before the season's final ferry. At the platform he turns around. Emotional beat: choice made in the body before the mind agrees.

chapters.title: Answered
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Dominic appears at her door soaked from the walk, carrying her unsent letter, which he found in the mailbox, and answers it aloud: every word was true except the signature. Emotional beat: vulnerability as arrival.

chapters.title: Climax: The Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Harrow, furious at losing the land deal, forces an emergency ruling; the couple races the tide to the dock, petition signatures in hand, and boards the final ferry to deliver them to the regional office before the appeal deadline. Emotional beat: everything risked at once.

chapters.title: Winter Residents
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The appeal succeeds; the lighthouse and mailbox are protected. Dominic signs the lease renewal on his workshop; Petra signs hers on the cottage. They hang a shared mailbox between the houses. Emotional beat: home as a decision, renewed daily.

chapters.title: Epilogue: Yours, D.
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. One year later, Dominic plans a small wedding—not for clients, but their own, on the lighthouse steps. He leaves one last letter in the box for Petra to find: a proposal, signed with his full name. Emotional beat: inheritance transformed—what was hidden becomes legacy.
